newsitem.title: USA: Dow index dips but holds above 6,000 for second day.
newsitem.headline: Dow index dips but holds above 6,000 for second day.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average ended slightly lower Tuesday but managed to hold above the 6,000 level for the second day, while the technology-laden Nasdaq index set its second straight record high.
The Dow was off 5.22 points at 6,004.78. In the broader market, declining issues led advances 1,301 to 1,058 on heavy volume of 458 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
"We're up 450 points in five weeks and 850 since July 16. We have a new millenium of 6,000 and a lot of good news," said Alfred Goldman, technical research director of A.G. Edwards.
"We've come a long way in a short time ... The odds favour a pause to refresh and then work higher," he said.
The Nasdaq Composite index notched another record closing high, gaining 1.74 points to 1,258.10 as the shares of Intel Corp. surged on a 40 percent jump in third-quarter profits.
Intel ended with a gain of 3-1/2 at 111-1/8 after trading at a 52-week high of 114-1/4.
Analysts said stocks were searching for a catalyst before making further inroads into record ground.
The market's recent gains were fuelled by the outlook for continued moderate economic growth and low inflation, which should help corporate earnings.

"We had a market inspired early in the day by Intel and although Intel has not given up most of its gains, most tech measures have and turned in bouts of profit-taking," said Joseph Barthel, chief investment strategist of Fahnestock & Co.
"There was a similar profile among bank stocks. They had on-target or slightly better-than-expected quarterly results by a penny or two," he said.
Among those reporting, Chase Manhattan was unchanged at 82-1/2, Citicorp rose 1-1/4 to 94-5/8 and First Chicago NBD was up 1-5/8 to 48-1/4.
"The market is tired and needs another catalyst to get it over," Barthel said. "It could be delivered by CPI but I'm not certain the number has been somewhat discounted."
The Consumer Price Index for September is set for release Wednesday with economists expecting an increase of 0.3 percent vs. a 0.1 percent rise in the prior month.
Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities, said stocks were helped and hindered by earnings surprises.
Bay Networks lost 3-1/8 to 20-7/8 after reporting a drop in its quarterly income and the resignation of its chief executive.

Intel's earnings report did little to buoy other computer chip makers but boosted the stocks of personal computer makers. Compaq rose 3-1/4 to 75-1/8, Dell Computer added 3-1/2 to 88-3/8 and Gateway 2000 was up 3-3/8 to 56-3/4.

Companies moving higher after posting stronger quarterly results included Clorox, up 3-7/8 to 101-5/8, Caterpillar, up 2-1/4 to 76-3/8, General Motors, up 1/4 to 52-1/8, and Chips & Technologies, up 4-7/8 to 19-3/4.
U.S. Robotics gained 8-7/8 to 78 on news that it will unveil a new technology on Wednesday.
Conrail Inc. gained 14-1/8 to 85-1/8 after CSX Corp. agreed to merge with Conrail in an $8.4 billion deal. The pact values Conrail at $92.50 a share. CSX lost 2-3/4 to 46-3/4.
Norfolk Southern surged 3 to 95 and other railroads rose on hopes for further consolidation.

FlightSafety International jumped 5-3/8 to 49-1/4 after Berkshire Hathaway agreed to acquire the provider of training programmes for aircraft pilots and technicians for either $50 a share in cash or $48 a share in stock.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 0.97 to 702.57. The American Stock Exchange index was off 3.68 to 575.65.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 0.63 to 373.60. The average share was down 7 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 6,891.424 down 5.151 or 0.07 percent.
